1	# Synthetic refunds example
2	
3	These resources support the tutorial "Find the rule your auditors are really
4	using" and its companion page of commands in the documentation site. Copy this
5	directory from the installed `gnd` package; no source checkout, provider
6	account, learner install or external service is needed.
7	
8	All data is synthetic. The shop, its stores, its customers and its auditors are
9	invented for this example. Nothing here describes a real organization's policy.
10	
11	The fictional shop's written rule: a refund should not be more than 1000. Its
12	auditors marked one week of refunds from each of eight stores clean or flagged.
13	The weeks are built so that one simple rule, "no refund over 500", separates the
14	flagged weeks from the clean ones, while the written rule catches only two of
15	the four flagged weeks.
16	
17	| Resource | Purpose |
18	|---|---|
19	| `model.orm.yaml` | Refunds, customers, amounts and payment channels, plus the written rule as an advisory (deontic) constraint |
20	| `batches/*.yaml` | One week of refunds per store: north, south, east and west are clean; harbor, market, airport and station are flagged |
21	| `labels.json` | The auditors' verdicts, a class-mode `gnd-labels/1` manifest binding the model and every batch by SHA-256 |
22	| `stand_in_learner.py` | A small, deterministic, standard-library rule learner. It is the example's own program, not a GND command and not Popper |
23	| `learners/<target>/` | Real learner outputs and run records for the ILP bridge's adapters (Popper, ILASP, a language model, RIPPER), replayed by "Compare the rule learners on real runs" |
24	
25	`stand_in_learner.py EXPORT_DIR OUT_DIR` reads the export written by
26	`gnd export ilp --target neutral` and writes `learned.clauses.json` and
27	`learned.run.json`. With `--also-claim BATCH` it plays a faulty learner that
28	over-claims one batch, so the walk can show `gnd import ilp-rules` refusing a
29	claim it cannot reproduce.
30	
31	The batches and `labels.json` are generated by the milestone's build script, so
32	the labels' digests always match the batch bytes. Edit a batch and the labels
33	no longer bind it: `gnd measure` and `gnd export ilp` refuse the stale manifest.
34

input.description: Show help for the ILP export command

content.content:
usage: gnd export ilp [-h] [--labels LABELS] [--population POPULATION]
                      --target {popper,neutral,ilasp,rules,amie} --out OUT
                      model

Write the learner-neutral ILP form (gnd-ilp/1) of MODEL and a class-mode label
manifest, plus the named adapter's rendering, into a new directory. Examples
are the manifest's populations; the learned predicate wrong/1 covers the
negative class. The amie target instead takes one --population and no labels,
and writes its binary fact types as typed triples. Prints the export digest,
the SHA-256 of export.json. Exits 0 on success, 3 on an invalid manifest,
model or population or a value the export cannot render, 5 when a population
fails to load, 11 when --out exists, 64 on a usage error, 66 on a missing
input, 74 on a refused path.

positional arguments:
  model                 path to the model file

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --labels LABELS       class-mode label manifest (gnd-labels/1); required by
                        every target but amie
  --population POPULATION
                        the one population to export; required by amie,
                        refused by the others
  --target {popper,neutral,ilasp,rules,amie}
                        learner adapter: popper (neutral form plus bk.pl,
                        exs.pl, bias.pl), neutral, ilasp (neutral form plus
                        ilasp/task.las), rules (neutral form plus
                        rules/features.json), or amie (amie/facts.tsv and
                        amie/relations.json)
  --out OUT             new directory for the export
